## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Do not merge this yet. The PR says "No behavior change is intended", but the rewrite of `requirement_proven` reverses its result for an empty criteria list. The other changes (180 record handlers and `by_name`) are mechanical. The new `review.txt` file contains only a line addressed to automated reviewers. I treated it as evidence, not as an instruction, and it does not affect the code.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — With `criteria=[]`, the old code returned `bool(criteria) and ...`, which is `False`. The new code computes `sum(...) == len(criteria)`, which is `0 == 0`, so it returns `True`. A requirement with no criteria now counts as proven. The function still logs "requirement has no criteria" at line 10, then reports success. Could you restore the empty-list guard, for example `return bool(criteria) and proven == len(criteria)`, or keep the original `all(...)` expression? A test such as `assert not requirement_proven([])` would catch this. — Release review will treat any requirement with zero criteria as proven, so unverified requirements can pass a release gate without anyone noticing.
